  "text": "The library’s umbrella stand contained seven umbrellas, although it had not rained for nineteen days.

“People forget,” said Ruth, the librarian.

“Not for nineteen days,” said Mr Bell. “By then they’ve made a decision.”

He came every Tuesday to read the shipping news in a newspaper delivered on Friday. He had never been to sea.

Ruth put a notice above the stand: IS ONE OF THESE YOURS?

By Thursday, there were nine umbrellas.

“That’s an answer,” Mr Bell said.

She considered taking them to the charity shop, but the green one had a wooden handle worn smooth by somebody’s palm. The smallest had a name sewn inside, in stitching she could no longer read.

Instead, she changed the notice: PLEASE BORROW IF NEEDED.

Rain arrived on Monday.

By closing time, every umbrella had gone except a yellow one with a bent spoke.

Mr Bell stood at the door, buttoning his coat.

“Take it,” Ruth said.

“I live quite near.”

“The rain doesn’t know that.”

He opened it carefully. One side drooped over his shoulder.

“Rather private,” he said, and stepped outside.

The next Tuesday he returned it with the spoke repaired.

“Had some wire in a drawer.”

Soon the green umbrella came back too, followed by a black one Ruth didn’t recognise. Someone left a jar of sweets beneath the notice.

In December, Mr Bell missed a Tuesday.

On Wednesday, Ruth found the yellow umbrella missing and a note on the desk.

Borrowed for hospital visit. Back Friday.

She folded his newspaper and put it aside.

Then she added a few sweets, choosing the soft ones."
